required_stages.description: Obtain a non-aliasing output buffer of q's shape and dtype inside run(): an empty allocation (out-of-place) or a clone of q (in-place scheme).
Per (batch, position) row, read the cos and sin rows of the sequence position (row index modulo S), shared across heads.
One elementwise launch: for every head and i < D/2 read (q[i], q[i+D/2]) and write q1*cos - q2*sin to the first half and q2*cos + q1*sin to the second half of the output.

forbidden_substitutions.message: Host-side concatenation of the two halves reproduces the reference formulation outside the kernel.
Host-side broadcasting of the tables; combined with slicing arithmetic this performs the rotation in PyTorch.
Regenerating the rotary tables or using a complex-number formulation; the tables are inputs and must be consumed as given.
A library or reference-style rotary routine replaces the kernel.
Reference-style half slicing and tensor arithmetic on the host.
Mutating or returning the input q violates the no-mutation / fresh-output rules.
Interleaved (even/odd) pairing is a different operator; pairing must be i with i + D/2.

required_evidence.message: No kernel-level store found; the rotation must be done by a kernel.
No evidence of half-split addressing (element i paired with i + D/2).
No evidence that the table row is selected by the sequence position (row modulo S).

outputs.aliasing: none; the returned (B, S, H, D) tensor must be a buffer created inside run() (empty allocation or clone of q) and must not share storage with q, cos or sin

timing_boundary.notes: Everything inside run() is timed, including any clone of q used by an in-place scheme, the layout views, the output allocation and the rotation kernel. The tables are consumed as given; no cached state across calls, no table transformation or regeneration outside the kernel.
